Figure caption: Mechanism of mRNA vaccine-induced immunity. Following intramuscular administration, mRNA-LNP complexes are internalized by local antigen-presenting cells (APCs), such as dendritic cells. The acidic environment of the endosome triggers protonation of ionizable lipids, leading to endosomal disruption and release of mRNA into the cytoplasm. The mRNA is translated into antigenic protein, which is processed and presented via MHC I and MHC II pathways to activate CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, respectively. This triggers a potent adaptive immune response, including T cell-mediated cytotoxicity and B cell differentiation into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

Figure caption: Innovations in mRNA vaccine delivery systems. A comparison of traditional and novel delivery platforms. (A) Intramuscular injection using a conventional syringe. (B) Microneedle patches painlessly deliver vaccine to the immune-cell-rich dermis. (C) Jet injectors use a high-pressure stream for needle-free delivery. (D) Inhalable formulations target the respiratory mucosa, inducing localized immunity. These alternative systems aim to improve patient compliance, enable self-administration, reduce cold-chain dependence, and elicit mucosal immunity.
